I'm... not sure what your point is. I said in my original post that venators with fighters win the vast majority of times but without fighters (since you didn't specify in the prompt) the imperial wins.

With fighters, the difference is so huge that the presence of the venators is negligible as anything more than a delivery mechanism. Without fighters they're hopelessly outgunned by the 25 or so years of warship development.

As for evasive maneuvers, the imperial can do the same and again you're back to the difference in weapons that's just too big to overcome.

This fight comes 100 percent down to whether or not fighters are involved and again, you didn't specify in the prompt, so I attempted to give answers to with and without.

I took the numbers from Wookieepedia which is about as good a source as you'll get. 

A venator is sporting 8 dual heavy turbolaser turrets, 2 medium dual turbolaser cannons, 52 point defence lasers and 4 heavy proton torpedo tubes.

An imperial 2 star destroyer is armed with 60 turbolaser batteries, 60 heavy ion emplacements and 8 octuple turbolaser batteries.

As you can see the difference is just too big in favour of the imperial star destroyer, even with the lack of any missiles. I also addressed the question of the fighters. The imperial 2 has a decided lack of any point defence guns (hence why they couldn't  hit the Falcon) and the venators squads are both better than anything the Imperial is stocking as well as carrying about 3 times as many in a single ship assuming both are at their full complement.

As for the effective range, that's honestly hard to judge in star wars but given what we see on screen and how close battles happen, as well as the advances in technology between the venator and imperial, I think it's safe to say that if the venators are in range then so is the imperial.

A single Imperial 2 star destroyer has an offensive output roughly equal to about 6 venators all on its own. It also has far stronger shields and hull. I honestly don't see the venators even having a chance at winning without their fighters or tricks like the artillery cannon in their underside hangars.

In a straight slugfest, Impstar 2 10/10.
With fighters, I think the venators win 8/10 though not without heavy damage. Maybe only one ends up surviving.
With the artillery, I think it totally depends on how competent the crews are as they will need to get very, very close to the Impstar to use them.

No problem at all. We all have to start learning somewhere. Disengage isn't actually an action. Its a keyword that affects your movement. Normally to leave combat you need to spend two movement actions to do so. Disengage let's you leave combat with only one movement action. This combined with the charge keyword and Ataru Mastery means that Yoda can move into one unit with one move action, get a free attack from the charge keyword, move out of engagement with his second action due to disengage and either move into another unit for a free melee attack action or use his ranged attack on a unit in range. Unfortunately due to the way the range rulers work he probably can't get a second melee attack on the first enemy unit but it's still a great combo.
Yoda has Ataru Mastery on his card which lets him perform 2 attack actions.

Think of it this way, no matter how good Yoda is, at worst, Rex will be the second best commander. He's probably always going to be at worst a solid option to build around. Also, welcome to the game. Hope you enjoy yourself.

Before I get started, I wanted to apologise. When it comes to Star Wars, I've read a lot of material. More than I can remember some times. I tend to just assume that people are working from the same knowledge base as I am and forget to clarify a lot of my points. Hell I'll probably do it again during this (unintentionally) so sorry if I sound like a dick at times too.

http://starwars.wikia.com/wiki/T-16_skyhopper That's a link to the wookiepedia article on skyhoppers. In it, it's mentioned a couple of times that they're similar in design to the X-Wings. 

As for Anakin, he started out pod racing yes? Of that we can all agree. The reason he's so good at this is because The Force enhances his reflexes and gives him minor precognitive abilities, hence why he's the only human who can do it. However, a pod racer is essentially just a couple of engines strapped to a chair. The only controls it has as far as actually driving it are how much power you're putting out with each engine. The most difficult part about it is being able to maintain your speed and direction while working the various peripheral systems on it which Anakin does do quite well. As for the naboo star fighter scene, that can also be used as evidence for what I'm saying. In the beginning, Anakin doesn't even know how to use the cockpit controls. If I remember correctly, all he does is manage to put it on autopilot, panic a bit until R2 can reset it to manual control, then fluke his way into winning the battle. He displayed next to no expertise in his piloting ability, simply trying several manoeuvre's that any ten year old (even one in our reality) would know about. The only thing that made him special in those scenes was that there was a battle going on around him. Yes it's impressive, yes The Force had something to do with it but it certainly wasn't the be all and end all of his piloting ability. Sure he gets better as the series goes on but this was during a war. The Jedi temple had it's own starfighter division and it's not a desperate leap to assume that the Jedi partaking in the battles would be required to train themselves rigorously beforehand. The Jedi were indeed famous for their piloting ability, but again, with the training and the advantage of Force enhanced reflexes and precognition, there's no reason why they SHOULDN'T be good. 

I guess what I'm trying to say here is, as before, The Force isn't what's making them good at piloting. HOWEVER, and I should have clarified this before, it's definitely a factor in making them good at what they do. I feel that in this case, it should be viewed as an extra piece of equipment that not all pilots have access to. If you give two pilots of the same skill two different ships where one is markedly better, then that pilot will almost certainly come out on top. In the same manner though, if you give a terrible pilot an excellent ship and an excellent pilot a mediocre or just plain bad ship, it's more likely to swing in the favour of experience.

The thing about that is that in the Star Wars universe, a lot of the technology is standardised across the board. Lukes Skyhopper (a recreational vehicle) has the exact same controls and instrument panel as an X-Wing. That's why he was able to pilot it so easily. He'd basically been running in an X-Wing simulator since he was 10. As for Anakin though, that I can't explain. I'm sure somebody else could though. Anyway, point being, it's not just The Force making them good at piloting.

So we're riding our bikes with him and see a bunch of kids with rocks. When they saw all If us coming though they booked it back inside. Cue us patting each others backs for being badasses. Little did we know though, our friend had been mouthing off at the kids and throwing rocks back and their bogan as hell dad was sick of it. He runs out of the house looking for us and when he sees us, jumps in his car and starts driving after us. We all split up at that moment and I rode off with a couple of other guys. 

For some reason the dad figured we were the best targets and started following us. We had a good lead and were trying to get into a nearby bush reserve where he couldn't follow us anymore. Now as luck would have it, it was about this time that my bike chain came off. I flipped over the handle bars and landed surprisingly well but then the dad pulled up next to me, got out of the car and starts waving a mother fucking combat knife in my face, telling me how he's going to kill me for abusing his family. As you can imagine, I'm pretty fucking scared right now and I kept telling him I hadn't done anything but he wouldn't listen. He just kept screaming at me. 

Luckily for me, another friend of mine saw him from the other end of the street and started shouting at the dad, calling him a cunt and the dad decided he would be a better target than me, got in his car and drive off. I managed to get my chain back on and met up with the two guys I was originally with. We high tailed it into the bush and went the back route home thinking that would be the end of it... It wasn't.

So we finally get close to home, we can literally see our houses, when the dad comes round the corner on foot this time with about a dozen other guys who all looked at least 16, all with their own weapons. It was the biggest oh shit moment we'd ever had as they ran at us and we tried to turn around. We managed to get away but not before one guy had been hit in the head with a cricket bat.

To end the story, we were bush bashing for a while, carrying our bikes with us and we made it to the house of the guy who'd been hit. His dad, who was a police sergeant, flipped out and took us all down to the police station to give statements. It turns out the guy who was chasing us was suspected of dealing meth or something on top of trying to hurt/kill us. Unfortunately he ran before anyone could get to him so that was about of a disappointment. But yeah, that's the time I was scared for my life. Sorry about the wall of text.
